q: All theories of physics developed before the arrival of relativity and quantum mechanics and any work derived from them are called ____.
e: All theories of physics developed before the arrival of relativity and quantum mechanics and any work derived from them are called classical physics. Classical physics here means physics built before relativity and quantum mechanics.

q: On the other hand, the theories derived from the basic principles of relativity and quantum mechanics which are two pillars of physics today, are called ____.
e: On the other hand, the theories derived from the basic principles of relativity and quantum mechanics which are two pillars of physics today, are called modern physics. Modern physics here means physics built on relativity and quantum mechanics.

q: The word modern was chosen since the main foundations of the two pillars of physics were laid in the first three decades of the ____.
e: The word modern was chosen since the main foundations of the two pillars of physics were laid in the first three decades of the twentieth century. The physics in this sentence is built around twentieth century.

q: The process by which, free electrons are emitted from the surface of a metal when external heat energy is applied, is called ____.
e: The process by which, free electrons are emitted from the surface of a metal when external heat energy is applied, is called thermionic emission. Heat frees electrons from the cathode, and they travel through vacuum to the anode. Heat is energy on the move; it is not the same word as temperature.

q: Thermionic emission occurs in metals that are heated to a very ____.
e: Thermionic emission occurs in metals that are heated to a very high temperature. High temperature here means how hot or cold a body is. Heat frees electrons from the cathode, and they travel through vacuum to the anode.

q: Vacuum diode is the simplest form of ____.
e: Vacuum diode is the simplest form of vacuum tube. Vacuum tube here means a space emptied of air so electrons can travel freely in a tube. Heat frees electrons from the cathode, and they travel through vacuum to the anode.

q: It consists of two electrodes, a cathode and an anode (or) ____.
e: It consists of two electrodes, a cathode and an anode (or) plate. Heat frees electrons from the cathode, and they travel through vacuum to the anode.

q: The cathode emits the free electrons by ____.
e: The cathode emits the free electrons by thermionic emission. Heat frees electrons from the cathode, and they travel through vacuum to the anode.
The anode collects the electrons. Heat frees electrons from the cathode, and they travel through vacuum to the anode.

q: A vacuum diode is used as an AC (alternative current) to DC (direct current) ____.
e: A vacuum diode is used as an AC (alternative current) to DC (direct current) converter. Heat frees electrons from the cathode, and they travel through vacuum to the anode.

q: Nowadays, vacuum tubes are obsolete, having been replaced by transistors and ____.
e: Nowadays, vacuum tubes are obsolete, having been replaced by transistors and semiconductor diodes. Semiconductor diodes here means a material with a moderate number of free electrons. A semiconductor sits between a conductor and an insulator.
